Preventive care refers to health services aimed at avoiding or reducing the onset, severity, and complications of diseases and injuries. It includes primary prevention, such as vaccinations and health promotion to reduce risks before illness occurs, and secondary prevention, such as screenings to detect diseases early and enable timely treatment. In the System of Health Accounts, preventive care is limited to these two levels and excludes tertiary prevention, which is considered part of curative or rehabilitative care.
Preventive services not elsewhere classified because the specific programme type (e.g., IEC, immunisation, screening, surveillance, preparedness) cannot be identified from the source.

Other medical durable goods include all medical non-durable products acquired by patients, regardless of where they are purchased other than prescribed medicines (HC.5.1.1) and over-the-counter medicines (HC.5.1.2). This category excludes veterinary products and items for personal hygiene, such as medicinal soaps, but includes traditional, complementary and alternative medicine (TCAM) goods when classified as medical products, while excluding items like “healthy food” that are not recognised as medical goods.

nodes.value: Medical goods (non-specified by function) refers to the consumption of medicines and other medical products that are not linked to a specific health care function such as prevention, cure, rehabilitation or long-term care. These goods may be provided within health care facilities or purchased independently through retailers, including cases of self-prescription. The category also captures situations where patients or their families must buy medicines directly, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, and recognises the growing role of independent consumption across diverse distribution channels.

Count_Product_MobileCellularSubscription.label: Mobile Phone Subscriptions Per Person in a Population

nodes.value: Mobile Phone Subscriptions Per Person in a Population

Mobile cellular telephone subscriptions are subscriptions to a public mobile telephone service that provide access to the PSTN using cellular technology. The indicator includes (and is split into) the number of postpaid subscriptions, and the number of active prepaid accounts (i.e. that have been used during the last three months). The indicator applies to all mobile cellular subscriptions that offer voice communications. It excludes subscriptions via data cards or USB modems, subscriptions to public mobile data services, private trunked mobile radio, telepoint, radio paging and telemetry services. International Telecommunication Union, World Telecommunication/ICT Development Report and database.

nodes.value: Inward Remittances as a Percentage of Nominal Gross Domestic Production

Personal remittances comprise personal transfers and compensation of employees. Personal transfers consist of all current transfers in cash or in kind made or received by resident households to or from nonresident households. Personal transfers thus include all current transfers between resident and nonresident individuals. Compensation of employees refers to the income of border, seasonal, and other short-term workers who are employed in an economy where they are not resident and of residents employed by nonresident entities. Data are the sum of two items defined in the sixth edition of the IMF's Balance of Payments Manual: personal transfers and compensation of employees. World Bank staff estimates based on IMF balance of payments data, and World Bank and OECD GDP estimates.

nodes.value: Personal remittances comprise personal transfers and compensation of employees. Personal transfers consist of all current transfers in cash or in kind made or received by resident households to or from nonresident households. Personal transfers thus include all current transfers between resident and nonresident individuals. Compensation of employees refers to the income of border, seasonal, and other short-term workers who are employed in an economy where they are not resident and of residents employed by nonresident entities. Data are the sum of two items defined in the sixth edition of the IMF's Balance of Payments Manual: personal transfers and compensation of employees. Data are in current U.S. dollars. World Bank staff estimates based on IMF balance of payments data.
